fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK/PHB display against competing background lighting is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue directly tied to drivers detecting the beacon and yielding to crossing pedestrians.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (drivers confused by competing background elements at night at this location) is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-001 traced to the FHWA Tucson case study issue table.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern rather than a compliance question under FHWA RSA practice, with no conflation of MUTCD compliance obligations and site-specific safety judgment.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border on the signal backplate is a specific, location-pinned, low-cost and implementable countermeasure at final design, consistent with FHWA conspicuity treatments.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users should drivers misread or detect the beacon late, linking driver conspicuity to VRU protection.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing adequate for slower walkers at high-collision-frequency HAWK sites is a genuine, substantive VRU safety issue addressable at final design stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Verbatim quote from EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') directly supports the pivotal claim for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety concern under FHWA RSA semantics, not conflated with any MUTCD compliance question, and scoped to the final-design stage where timing remains adjustable.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all six named sites), actionable (reprogramme clearance intervals), and viable via reduced assumed walking speed; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly named as affected road users and are the central focus of both the concern and the verification request.
